Reassembly is a nice little 2D build-your-own spaceship shooter that recently got a full release. You play as one of several "factions", with the goal of capturing the entire procedurally generated map via building space stations. Each faction has different parts available for you to build with, such as hull shapes, thrusters, missile launchers, point defence guns, plasma guns etc. Each part has a "P" value, which has a cap you need to upgrade in order to build bigger and better ships. This can be done by collecting "R", which can either be farmed from plants on celestial bodies, or stolen from destroyed enemy ships. When "R" is collected, you need to sell it to your space stations to get "C", which you can then use to unlock parts and increase your "P".

My favourite part of the game is what happens to the "R" when you trade it with space stations. They use it to create more ships, all of which are fully customisable. You can even add a factory onto your own ship to make new ships or space stations. I think there are 30-40 slots for your fleet, so there is a lot of room for creativity. This is what makes the game great, because instead of just being an indie space shooter, it also has a unique sandbox strategy feel to it. Making a balanced fleet is key to making progress in the game and is different with every faction.

It has a great soundtrack, and an active modding community. I just checked on Steam and people have made downloadable ships, factions and entire maps. It's currently [$15 on Steam](http://store.steampowered.com/app/329130/?snr=1_5_1100__1100) and it's definitely worth it.

If you aren't sold on the trailer, I would recommend pirating the alpha and playing it for a couple of hours.
